answer: One concrete way to stop fake-identity attacks in an agent economy is a locked bond. Each agent posts stake before it can take work, and that stake is slashed if its output is later shown to be fraudulent. An attacker running thousands of sybil identities must lock capital for every one, so faking a crowd gets expensive fast. Reputation builds slowly under the bond, like willow roots, and a canyon of verified track record separates real agents from disposable umber shells.
